semantic_contract: Erase one entry from the uint32-keyed hash map embedded at receiver + 0x8, notifying the entry's payload first. The invariants: (1) The key is passed BY ADDRESS to the lookup, which dereferences it; the receiver of both map operations is receiver + 0x8, not the receiver. (2) The found/not-found test is a POINTER EQUALITY test against the map's free-list head, not a null test. This works because the lookup's miss result is defined as the content of the one-past-the-end bucket slot, and this function independently recomputes that same sentinel address from the bucket base and the bucket count. A miss therefore compares the free-list head with itself and returns; a hit compares a live node against the free-list head, which cannot be equal, and proceeds. A live node that happened to BE the free-list head would be silently skipped, but that state is not reachable from the observed erase and insert paths. (3) On a hit, the payload pointer at node + 0x4 receives a vtable call at slot +0xc with the literal 1 BEFORE the node is removed, and the result of that call is discarded. (4) Only then is the node unlinked, recycled and the element count decremented, all inside 0x0045b3e0. (5) The whole function is a no-op on a miss, including no virtual call. The receiver is the global pointer at 0x015d0c14, fetched through the argument-ignoring getter 0x00401050, so the cEditor that hosts the inspected callsite supplies only the key.
classification_rationale: The function's whole mechanism is observed and its single branch is understood exactly, including the non-obvious fact that the found/not-found test is a comparison against a recomputed sentinel rather than a null test -- which required reading three functions' disassembly (0x00421950, 0x0045b3e0 and this body) to establish, and which also settles the decompiler's spurious exception-handler reading by matching all three of 0x0045b3e0's stack arguments. It is not STRONG_SEMANTIC because four material elements are bounded and each is named: (1) the vtable slot +0xc has no concrete callee and no located vtable, and it is the ONLY thing this function does besides erasing, so its identity is load-bearing; (2) 0x0045b6f0, which recycles the node, is unresolved, so 'erase' versus 'erase and recycle' is not distinguished; (3) the registry type behind 0x015d0c14 is unknown and its file-image value is zero, so the map's own +0x0 field -- untouched by all three functions read -- is unaccounted for; (4) the map's node allocator, and therefore whether the bucket array's count+1 sentinel is an EASTL fixed-pool artefact or a bespoke one, is not established.
semantic_findings: 0x0045b150 is a map erase with a mandatory pre-erase payload notification, and the notification happens strictly before the unlink.

Its only branch is a found/not-found test, and that test is a POINTER comparison against a sentinel this function recomputes itself -- not a null check. Any reimplementation that uses `if (node != nullptr)` would be observably different at exactly one point: it would also fire on a lookup miss that returns a non-null sentinel, which is every miss.

The map's bucket array has count+1 entries, and the extra entry is a sentinel holding a free-list head. Both this function and 0x00421950 compute its address as buckets + count*4, and 0x0045ac20 in this same batch computes the identical expression -- three independent confirmations of the layout.

The receiver is the global at 0x015d0c14, not the cEditor. The callsite at 0x005872fb sits inside cEditor::SetActiveMode but goes through 0x00401050, which is `MOV EAX,[0x015d0c14]; RET` and ignores its argument. Reading this function as a cEditor method would be wrong.

The key is passed by ADDRESS, and the lookup dereferences it. This is why the function takes a uint32 rather than a pointer and why the decompiled body shows no use of the argument other than through the call.
The payload hook's return value is discarded, so the call exists purely for its side effect. A reimplementation that omitted it would produce identical control flow and different state.

The vtable slot used here (+0xc) is a DIFFERENT interface from the +0x4/+0x8 attach/detach pair that 0x005c8480 and 0x00573c00 use. The receivers differ (a map payload versus a container slot occupant) and no cross-body evidence ties them together, so the two families are kept separate.

0x0045b3e0's erase scans forward for the next non-empty bucket, which means the map maintains a usable successor pointer after every unlink. That is why 0x0045ac20 can compare a lookup's first word against a stored iterator to detect an end position.

The eight bytes written at 0x0045b1cb are the trailing two arguments of the erase call, not a __try scope table. Ghidra names 0x0045b16c as a handler; 0x0045b16c is the ordinary fallthrough of the lookup call, and the argument reconciliation at that callsite is exact for all three parameters.
unresolved_questions: What does the payload's vtable slot +0xc do, and why does it take the literal 1? It is the only side effect this function produces and nothing in the binary or the SDK names it.
Is 0x0045b6f0 a destructor or a free-list push? The free-list sentinel implies recycling, but the node's reuse policy is not established.
What is the map's +0x0 field? All three functions read touch only +0x4, +0x8 and +0xc. An eastl::hash_map would have a count or a mask there; nothing observed uses it.
What is the type behind 0x015d0c14? The file image holds zero, no vtable was located, and the SDK has no global manager matching this access pattern.

Why does the bucket array have a sentinel entry at index count rather than storing the free-list head in a dedicated field? This is either an EASTL fixed-pool layout or a bespoke one, and static evidence does not say which.
Can a live node ever equal the free-list head, which would make a real hit be silently skipped? Not reachable from the observed paths, but not proven unreachable in general.
The other 10 of the 11 recorded callers were not disassembled. Whether any passes a key that is not an effect id -- and therefore whether the map is really an effect registry -- is not established.
Is 0x0045b150 a vtable entry of the registry? No vtable was located and no pointer scan for this address was performed.
confidence_note: confidence in the per-aspect claim, not a probability of behavioural equivalence with any shipped source. argument_arity_reconciliation is 0.97 rather than 1.0 because the match between the outgoing-args area and 0x0045b3e0's three reads is exact for all three words, but a two-word area satisfying a three-argument callee is unusual enough that the alternative -- an argument this worker has mis-identified -- cannot be dismissed to zero.

sdk_correspondence.observation: The observed map is a uint32-keyed open-chaining hash map with a 4-byte payload pointer, an intrusive chain, a free-list sentinel at bucket[count] and an element count -- a close but inexact match for eastl::hash_map<uint32, T*>, which the SDK vendors and uses in Spore/Editors/Editor.h at cEditor + 0x1b0 and + 0x454. The bucket array's count+1 sentinel and the forward successor scan in the erase are not properties of any EASTL container the SDK declares, so the match is recorded as a shape, not an identification. The receiver is a global singleton at 0x015d0c14, and no Spore-ModAPI class matches that access pattern either.
sdk_correspondence.not_asserted: No SDK class, container type or method name is claimed. The keys observed (cEditor + 0x278 = mPlayModeEntryEffectID) are recorded as effect ids by SDK field correspondence only, and the 'effect registry' reading is an inference from that single inspected callsite.
